fact: The Swan's tail — one of the most luminous stars the eye can see, shining from far across the galaxy.
bio: Deneb (Alpha Cygni) is a blue-white supergiant so distant — likely well over a thousand light-years — that its brilliance in our sky implies a true luminosity tens of thousands of times the Sun's, among the most powerful stars visible without a telescope.
cultural: The name comes from the Arabic for 'tail', marking the tail of Cygnus the Swan. Deneb anchors the Summer Triangle with Vega and Altair and rides the length of the Milky Way's northern stream.
